title: Treasury Standard — Assembly of Capital Credit Payouts, Offsets and Minimums
content:
# Assembly of Capital Credit Payouts, Offsets and Minimums

**Product:** Capital Credits (Patronage Capital), every patron class.

## 1. Retired clause

The clause "Payouts are assembled per member, not per capital account." is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis and is not applied.

## 2. Clauses in force

2.1 **Combination.** At each payout, the retired credits owed on all of the member's capital accounts — the total payable balance across every capital account of the same member on the payout date — are combined.

2.2 **Offset first.** Where the patron class applies retirements first to unpaid final-billed balances (every class does), the combined amount is first applied to the member's unpaid final-billed balances — the positive balances, on the payout date, of the member's service accounts in final billed status — oldest final balance first. Each offset is posted as a separate offset payout against that service account, and appears on that service account as a bill credit for a capital credit offset.

2.3 **One payout of the remainder.** What remains is paid in one payout: a bill credit to the member's oldest active service account in the class when the member is active and the class pays active members by bill credit; otherwise one check to the mailing address on file. A bill-credit payout appears on the service account as a bill credit for a capital credit retirement.

2.4 **Minimums and carry-forward.** A payout is made only when the combined remainder is at least the class's smallest bill-credit payout for a bill credit, or the class's smallest check payout for a check. Where the class carries payables forward (every class does), a smaller remainder stays payable and is added to the next payout. The class figures are $1.00 for a bill credit in every class, and $10.00 for a check in every class except the Large Power Patron Class, where it is $25.00.

2.5 **Open accounts are not offset.** An unpaid balance on an open, active service account is never offset; it is collected under the Electric Service by Rate Schedule rules.

2.6 **Inactive members and estates.** An inactive member and an estate are always paid by the method the class sets for inactive members and estates, which is a check in every class.

These conditions are read from the system records of the member's capital accounts and service accounts on the payout date.

## 3. Worked illustration (hypothetical figures, Residential Patron Class)

An inactive member is owed $42.50 on one capital account and $8.30 on another, combined $50.80. The member's service accounts show two final-billed balances: $30.00 on the account final billed first and $12.00 on the account final billed later.

| Step of the rule | Amount |
|---|---|
| Combined payable | $50.80 |
| Offset against the older final balance | $30.00 |
| Offset against the later final balance | $12.00 |
| Remainder | $8.80 |
| Payout by check | none — $8.80 is below $10.00 and stays payable for the next payout |

Had the member also owed $1.20 more, the remainder would have been exactly $10.00 and one check of $10.00 would have been mailed.

superseded_clauses: Payouts are assembled per member, not per capital account.
